milestones.description:
How The Engagement Will Work
The Council will conduct a two-stage preliminary market engagement.
Stage 1 will share details of the heat network and the current reference design work, so that interested parties can explore the opportunity and the Council can obtain feedback on the scheme proposal. It will comprise of a one-hour webinar presented by the Council on Wednesday 18 November 2026 at 12 noon, held online via Microsoft Teams.
Stage 2 is expected to be held in February or March 2027 and will be supported by a more detailed Project Information Document. This stage will include in person presentation, meetings at Hounslow House and a site visit to Thames Water's Mogden Sewage Waste Water Works and West Middlesex University Hospital.
How To Take Part
If your organisation is interested in becoming the Council's Heat Network Development Partner and wishes to take part, please register your interest via the Council's eTendering portal https://procontract.due-north.com/Advert?advertId=cd2c8a30-93d7-f111-8142-6045bdf14b1f&fromProjectDashboard=True by 23:59 on Monday 16 November 2026 where a link is provided to the webinar. Questions may be submitted via the portal before and after the engagement up to the deadline of 1pm on 4 December 2026. The Council and its advisers will respond via the portal. The webinar presentation, together with an anonymised record of questions, responses and any other relevant information shared during the engagement, excluding information identified as commercially sensitive, will be made available on the portal to all registered parties.
Related Opportunity
The Council is also procuring a partner for a Strategic Energy Partnership ("SEP") to help fund and deliver a diverse portfolio of energy projects and programmes across the borough. A separate preliminary market engagement notice has been published for that opportunity (Portal Ref: DN834966). Organisations may take part in either or both engagements.
Fair And Transparent Engagement
•	Taking part in this engagement is not a condition of taking part in any future procurement and will not give any organisation an advantage.
•	A summary of the questions, answers and key information shared at each stage will be published to all registered parties via the portal and included in any future procurement documents. Questions will be anonymised and commercially sensitive information will not be disclosed.
The Council is supported by Womble Bond Dickenson (UK) LLP, AECOM and Amberside Advisors. When registering, please declare any relationship with the Council, its officers or its advisers that could give rise to a conflict of interest.
Indicative Timetable
The indicative timetable for the Hounslow Heat Network engagement and procurement is as follows (subject to change):
Stage 1 Engagement
Preliminary market engagement notice published: Tuesday 3 Nov 2026
Registration deadline; webinar invitation and information pack issued: Monday 16 Nov 2026, 23:59pm
Webinar: Wednesday 18 Nov 2026, 12:00
Deadline for submission of questions: Wednesday 4 Dec 2026, 1pm
Publication of Stage 1 engagement feedback: By Thursday 15 Jan 2027
Stage 2 engagement
Stage 2 in person event including site visit (details to follow):  Feb/ Mar 2027
Procurement
Tender notice published with tender documentation: Spring 2027
The Council currently expects to use the competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, including stages of dialogue. The procedure will be confirmed in the tender notice and associated tender documents.
All communications will be via the Council's eTendering portal https://procontract.due-north.com/Advert?advertId=cd2c8a30-93d7-f111-8142-6045bdf14b1f&fromProjectDashboard=True.
_______________________________________________________________
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
This notice is not a call for competition or an invitation to tender and does not bind the Council to carry out a procurement process.
Information provided through this engagement is subject to change and does not represent final decisions or commitments.
The Council and its advisers are not liable for any costs that interested parties may incur in taking part in this preliminary market engagement.
Information submitted may be subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. Please identify any information you consider commercially sensitive. Personal data will be handled in line with the Council's privacy notice (https://www.hounslow.gov.uk/privacy-notice).
This engagement is carried out in compliance with sections 16 and 17 of the Procurement Act 2023.

tender.title: Hounslow Heat Network
tender.description:
Following Cabinet approval in December 2025, the London Borough of Hounslow ("the Council") intends to commence a procurement process in Spring 2027 to select a Heat Network Development Partner ("HNDP") to fund and deliver a district heating network across the borough (the "Hounslow Heat Network").
The Council proposes to partner with the HNDP through a Joint Venture with Golden Share.
Scheme Overview
The Hounslow Heat Network is a borough-wide low-carbon infrastructure programme to modernise and improve the resilience of heat supply across the borough. It is intended to be delivered in phases, starting with an anchor scheme using heat recovery from Thames Water's Mogden Waste Water Treatment Works and expanding in the future to serve public, commercial and residential customers across the borough.
•	Scale: the full build-out is expected to supply 484 GWh of annual heat demand through a 69 km network.
•	First phase (the reference scheme): 45 GWh annual heat demand through a 9.57km network with anchor loads, including West Middlesex University Hospital and new build and Council-owned assets.
•	Funding: the Council has secured £10.55m of Green Heat Network Fund ("GHNF") funding.
•	Strategic importance: identified by the Greater London Authority ("GLA") as a strategically valuable heat network area. Hounslow is also part of the National Zoning pipeline, having secured DESNZ funding to form a Zone Coordination Body for the borough and surrounding area.
Who Should Take Part
The Council would like to hear from organisations with experience in the development, financing, construction and operation of heat networks, including those able to bring capital and delivery capability to the project. Consortia are welcome, as are smaller organisations interested in future supply chain opportunities.

tender.title: CTC Relocation Project
tender.description:
Weston College Group invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit a tender for the completion of the yielding-up, dismantling, removal, site clearance and restoration works required at the College's Construction Training Centre (CTC).
The works are required to facilitate the surrender of the site in accordance with planning obligations and landlord requirements and include the removal of modular buildings, associated structures, external works, below-ground services, foundations and hardstanding, together with reinstatement and restoration of the site. The programme of works is defined within the project master programme.
The successful contractor shall act as Principal Contractor under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 and shall coordinate the project works. Certain specialist works will be undertaken by contractors appointed directly by Weston College. The Principal Contractor shall provide access, coordination, supervision and contractor attendances as described within this specification.
tender.submissionMethodDetails: Responses must be submitted by email to AMTEC.procurement@weston.ac.uk by no later than 12pm, Monday 4 December 2026.

criteria.description: Tenders must provide responses using the ITT Form. The ITT can only be accessed following an Expression of Interest sent to AMTEC.procurement@weston.ac.uk. The college reserves the right to disqualify you if you do not submit your tender in a manner consistent with the provisions set out in Instructions to Tenderers, Specification, Terms and Conditions and the Tender Response Form.

awardCriteria.description:
Tender Evaluation and Award Criteria
7.1 Evaluation Methodology
Weston College Group will evaluate tenders on the basis of lowest compliant price.
Tenderers must submit a complete and compliant tender response in accordance with the requirements of this ITT. Only tenders deemed compliant with the requirements of the ITT will be considered for financial evaluation.
The evaluation process will comprise the following stages:
A. Compliance Assessment
All tender submissions will be reviewed to confirm that:
•	The tender has been completed in full
•	All requested information and supporting documentation have been provided
•	The Tenderer meets the minimum requirements of the ITT
•	The Tenderer's proposal complies with the specification, scope of works and contractual requirements
Weston College Group reserves the right to seek clarification of any aspect of a submission where necessary.
B. Financial Evaluation
A thorough analysis will be undertaken to determine the lowest compliant tender.
The submitted pricing schedule will be reviewed to ensure that all tenders are assessed on a comparable basis and that the prices submitted fully reflect the requirements of the works. Where necessary, Tenderers may be requested to provide clarification or supporting information to confirm the basis of their pricing.
C. Due Diligence
The Tenderer acknowledges and agrees that, as part of the evaluation process, Weston College Group reserves the right to undertake appropriate due diligence activities, including but not limited to:
•	Credit checks;
•	Financial standing assessments;
•	Reference checks; and
•	Other background verifications considered necessary by the College.
Tenderers shall cooperate fully with any reasonable requests for information or supporting documentation.
D. Tender Ranking and Award
Following completion of the compliance, financial and due diligence assessments, compliant tenders will be ranked in ascending order of tender price.
The contract will be awarded to the lowest priced compliant Tenderer, subject to:
•	Compliance with all mandatory requirements of the ITT;
•	Satisfactory due diligence outcomes; and
•	Confirmation that the submitted price fully reflects the scope of works and contract requirements.
7.2 Financial Evaluation
Cost Assessment
Tender prices will be reviewed to ensure that:
•	Prices have been submitted on a like-for-like basis;
•	The tender sum includes all costs associated with delivering the works described within this ITT;
•	Any exclusions, qualifications or assumptions are clearly identified; and
•	The submission represents a bona fide and deliverable offer.
The College reserves the right to seek clarification where pricing anomalies, omissions or qualifications are identified.
Tender Ranking
Compliant tenders will be ranked in accordance with their total tender price as follows:
Rank 1: Lowest compliant tender price
Rank 2: Second lowest compliant tender price
Rank 3: Third lowest compliant tender price
Subsequent Rankings: Remaining compliant tender prices in ascending order

tender.title: Health, Wellbeing and Night Hub
tender.description:
The Health, Wellbeing and Night Hub aims to deliver a preventative, integrated response for adults at risk of homelessness, rough sleeping, or poor health outcomes, particularly those discharged from hospital or unable to safely return to accommodation.
The service aims to:
•Prevent discharge to the street for eligible adults
•Provide immediate, short-term step-down support following hospital discharge
•Identify housing needs early and support move-on solutions
•Support access to appropriate services such as Housing and homelessness services,
•Provide welfare benefits and financial support.GP registration and health appointments (not exhaustive)
•Reduce rough sleeping and repeat homelessness
•Improve service user engagement with statutory and voluntary services

tender.description:
The Opportunity
Following Cabinet approval in December 2025, the London Borough of Hounslow ("the Council") intends to commence a procurement mid-late 2027 to select a Strategic Energy Partner ("the Partner") for a Strategic Energy Partnership ("SEP"). The Partner will help unlock investment and deliver a diverse portfolio of energy projects and programmes to drive the borough's energy transformation, accelerate decarbonisation and support the Council's net zero ambitions for both its own operations and estate and the wider borough.
An estimated £500m+ pipeline of energy infrastructure has been identified to support the borough's regeneration, growth and decarbonisation agenda. This includes building retrofit, renewable energy generation, vehicle fleet decarbonisation and EV charging infrastructure.
The Council aims to structure a commercially viable partnership that can fund, develop and deliver this pipeline in support of the borough's economic, social and environmental objectives. A key role of the Partner will be to identify and develop further pipeline opportunities and innovative energy solutions.
The partnership is intended as a long-term collaboration with the Council, the partnership and the respective roles of the Council and the Partner will be shaped by the feedback received through this engagement.
Who Should Take Part
The Council would like to hear from organisations with experience in large-scale or place-based energy, infrastructure or related sectors, including those able to bring capital and delivery capability to the partnership. Consortia are welcome, as are smaller organisations interested in future supply chain opportunities.

tender.title: Vehicle Repairs Service
tender.description:
Lancashire Constabulary’s Fleet Department require Accident/Collision and Vehicle Mechanical Repair Service to repair and maintain vehicles. The Authority is seeking to procure the services of between 5 and 8 suppliers to provide a broad range of repairs to Police Vehicles, to support our Vehicle Maintenance Strategies over a 2 year period, with the option to extend for a further 2 years.
The existing Lancashire Constabulary Vehicle Repairs Service Framework Agreement is due to expire 30th September 2027. The Constabulary will be replacing this with a new framework, estimated to start on 1st October 2027.
The estimated spend for the replacement framework will be in the region of £4 million.
Suppliers will need to be located within a 60-mile radius (via Google Maps) to our Headquarters site (PR4 5SB).  This will enable site visits for vehicle inspections and face to face contract management to take place at a location based within a distance that would not add unnecessary costs or delay to the service.
This criterion is also essential to meet carbon reduction and net zero targets, in addition to our obligation to reduce contract costs.
Suppliers outside of the specified radius are permitted to set up/utilise appropriate subcontracting arrangements within the radius. This can include the location and use of suitable sub-contractors who may be able to carry out this service on behalf of the supplier.
All vehicle repairs shall be completed strictly in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's latest repair methods, technical bulletins, approved repair procedures and specifications current at the time of repair.
Under no circumstances shall repair methods be used that deviate from manufacturer-approved processes unless written approval is obtained from the Lancashire Constabulary.
Qualifications that technicians undertaking repairs must possess include:
•	ATA Accreditation (or equivalent).
•	Manufacturer-specific training where available.
•	Evidence of ongoing CPD and technical updates.
Lancashire Constabulary will be conducting Pre-Market Engagement. Please keep an eye out for the UK2 Notice, and information included on our external websites.

additionalClassifications.description: Fleet management, repair and maintenance services

renewal.description: This contract is a 2 year contract, with the option to extend for a further 2 years.

This will enable site visits for vehicle inspections and face to face contract management to take place at a location based within a distance that would not add unnecessary costs or delay to the service.
This criterion is also essential to meet carbon reduction and net zero targets, in addition to our obligation to reduce contract costs.
Suppliers outside of the specified radius are permitted to set up/utilise appropriate subcontracting arrangements within the radius. This can include the location and use of suitable sub-contractors who may be able to carry out this service on behalf of the supplier.
All vehicle repairs shall be completed strictly in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's latest repair methods, technical bulletins, approved repair procedures and specifications current at the time of repair.
Under no circumstances shall repair methods be used that deviate from manufacturer-approved processes unless written approval is obtained from the Lancashire Constabulary.
Qualifications that technicians undertaking repairs must possess include:
•	ATA Accreditation (or equivalent).
•	Manufacturer-specific training where available.
•	Evidence of ongoing CPD and technical updates.
Lancashire Constabulary will be conducting Pre-Market Engagement. Please keep an eye out for the UK2 Notice, and information included on our external websites.

milestones.description:
How The Engagement Will Work
The Council will conduct a two-stage preliminary market engagement.
Stage 1 will allow interested parties and the Council to explore the SEP opportunity and share information to refine the partnership structure, approach and proposed pipeline. It will comprise:
•	a webinar presented by the Council on Wednesday 25 November 2026 at 12:00, held online via Microsoft Teams; and
•	one-to-one interviews with the Council and its advisors over a two-week period from Monday 7 December 2026 to 18 December 2026
Stage 2 is expected to take place in spring 2027 and will provide more detailed information on the proposed pipeline, the Council’s commercial development work and procurement approach.
How To Take Part
If your organisation is interested in becoming the Council’s Strategic Energy Partner and wishes to take part, please register your interest via the Council’s eTendering portal https://procontract.due-north.com/Advert?advertId=f38838eb-84d7-f111-8142-6045bdf14b1f by 23:59 on Monday 23 November 2026 where a link is provided to the webinar.
Market Engagement interviews
Interview slots are limited and will be prioritised to organisations intending to bid as the primary contractor or a lead specialist contractor.
A primary contractor would be contracting directly with the Council as the Partner, solely, leading a consortium or partnership. A lead specialist contractor for a key area of decarbonisation delivery or investment who would be part of a consortium or partnership. Participants must confirm their intention on the portal with their interview request.
Interviews are subject to a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), available on the portal. Invitations will be issued once the signed NDA has been uploaded on the portal. Members of a potential consortium or partnership are asked to attend a single interview together.
The Council welcomes feedback from across the market, including supply chain organisations, SMEs and VCSEs.
Questions may be submitted via the portal, before and after the engagement, up to the deadline in the timetable below. Interviewees will be subject to the confidentiality provisions of the NDA. The Council and its advisors will respond via the portal. The webinar presentation, together with an anonymised record of questions, responses and any other relevant information shared during the engagement, excluding information identified as commercially sensitive, will be made available on the portal to all registered parties.
Related Opportunity
The Council is also procuring a Heat Network Development Partner to fund and deliver a district heating network across the borough (the “Hounslow Heat Network”). A separate preliminary market engagement notice has been published for that opportunity (Portal Ref: DN834949). The Hounslow Heat Network is not being procured as part of the SEP.
Organisations may take part in either or both engagements.
Fair And Transparent Engagement
•	Taking part in this engagement is not a condition of taking part in any future procurement and will not give any organisation an advantage.
•	A summary of the questions, answers and key information shared at each stage will be published to all registered parties via the portal and included in any future procurement documents. Questions will be anonymised and commercially sensitive information will not be disclosed.
•	The Council is supported by Womble Bond Dickinson (UK) LLP and Amberside Advisors. When registering, please declare any relationship with the Council, its officers or its advisors that could give rise to a conflict of interest.
Indicative Timetable
The indicative timetable for the SEP engagement and procurement is as follows (subject to change):
Stage 1 engagement
Preliminary market engagement notice published: Tuesday 3 Nov 2026
Registration deadline; webinar invitation and information pack issued:	Monday 23 Nov 2026, 23:59
Webinar: Wednesday 25 Nov 2026, 12:00
One-to-one interviews: Monday 7 – Friday 18 Dec 2026
Deadline for submission of questions: Friday 18 Dec 2026, 1pm
Publication of Stage 1 engagement feedback: Thursday 14 Jan 2027
Stage 2 engagement
Stage 2 engagement event (details to follow): Q2 2027
Procurement
Tender notice published with full tender documentation: Q3 2027
The Council currently expects to use the competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, including stages of dialogue. The procedure will be confirmed in the tender notice and associated tender documents.
All communications will be via the Council’s eTendering portal https://procontract.due-north.com/Advert?advertId=f38838eb-84d7-f111-8142-6045bdf14b1f.
_______________________________________________________________
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
This notice is not a call for competition or an invitation to tender and does not bind the Council to carry out a procurement process.
Information provided through this engagement is subject to change and does not represent final decisions or commitments.
The Council and its advisers are not liable for any costs that interested parties may incur in taking part in this preliminary market engagement.
Information submitted may be subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. Please identify any information you consider commercially sensitive. Personal data will be handled in accordance with the Council’s privacy notice
(https://www.hounslow.gov.uk/privacy-notice).
This engagement is carried out in compliance with sections 16 and 17 of the Procurement Act 2023.

tender.title: Hounslow Strategic Energy Partnership
tender.description:
The Opportunity
Following Cabinet approval in December 2025, the London Borough of Hounslow (“the Council”) intends to commence a procurement mid-late 2027 to select a Strategic Energy Partner (“the Partner”) for a Strategic Energy Partnership (“SEP”). The Partner will help unlock investment and deliver a diverse portfolio of energy projects and programmes to drive the borough’s energy transformation, accelerate decarbonisation and support the Council’s net zero ambitions for both its own operations and estate and the wider borough.
An estimated £500m+ pipeline of energy infrastructure has been identified to support the borough’s regeneration, growth and decarbonisation agenda. This includes building retrofit, renewable energy generation, vehicle fleet decarbonisation and EV charging infrastructure.
The Council aims to structure a commercially viable partnership that can fund, develop and deliver this pipeline in support of the borough’s economic, social and environmental objectives. A key role of the Partner will be to identify and develop further pipeline opportunities and innovative energy solutions.
The partnership is intended as a long-term collaboration with the Council, the partnership and the respective roles of the Council and the Partner will be shaped by the feedback received through this engagement.
Who Should Take Part
The Council would like to hear from organisations with experience in large-scale or place-based energy, infrastructure or related sectors, including those able to bring capital and delivery capability to the partnership. Consortia are welcome, as are smaller organisations interested in future supply chain opportunities.

additionalClassifications.description: Steam, hot water and associated products
Heating, ventilation and air-conditioning installation work
Other sources of energy supplies and distribution

tender.title: Provision of Class 360 Maintenance/Refurbishment Moves
tender.description:
East Midlands Railway (EMR) operates a fleet of twenty-one (21) Class 360 Electric Multiple Units (EMUs) on services between Corby and London St Pancras. The fleet is maintained at Bedford Cauldwell Depot, with heavy maintenance activities and fleet refurbishment works undertaken at Siemens' Kings Heath Depot, Northampton.
The contract provides for the movement of Class 360 train units between Kettering Depot Sidings and Northampton Kings Heath Depot to support planned maintenance, overhaul and refurbishment activities. The contract also includes an option for train movements between Northampton Kings Heath Depot and Cricklewood A-E Sidings when required.
The Class 360 fleet comprises four-car electric multiple units of the Siemens Desiro Classic platform, fitted with Dellner 12 couplers and compatible braking control systems to facilitate movement operations.
The appointed supplier is responsible for the safe, reliable and efficient transportation of train units, including planning, coordination and delivery of movement services in accordance with all applicable railway safety requirements and operational standards.
Key objectives of the contract are:
Safe and damage-free movement of rolling stock.
Reliable and timely delivery of units to meet maintenance and operational schedules.
Efficient and cost-effective service provision.
Flexibility to accommodate changing operational requirements.
Minimisation of environmental impacts through efficient operational practices and resource utilisation.

additionalClassifications.description: Repair, maintenance and associated services related to aircraft, railways, roads and marine equipment

renewal.description: Option to extend: one extension period of up to 12 months following the initial 24-month term, exercisable at the Client's discretion subject to satisfactory performance and ongoing business requirements.

tender.title: Targeted Peer-Led Delivery of Needle and Syringe Provision and Harm Reduction
tender.description: Devon County Council is commissioning a Targeted Peer-Led Delivery of Needle and Syringe Provision and Harm Reduction Service. The Service seeks to reduce alcohol and other drug-related harm across Devon by leveraging the unique insights and trust of individuals with lived experience of substance use. Its primary aim is to provide an accessible, non-judgmental harm reduction service - including needle and syringe provision, Naloxone distribution, wound care, and blood-borne virus testing, through a peer-led model. By empowering peers to deliver education, support, and outreach, the Service's objectives are to decrease the transmission of blood-borne viruses, prevent overdoses, promote safer drug use practices, and foster a supportive community environment that encourages engagement with treatment and health services.
